stories.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
stories.hook: Would you keep believing someone who lied to you again and again?
stories.moral: The moral of the story is that no one believes a liar, even when they tell the truth.
stories.text: Would you keep believing someone who lied to you again and again? In a small green village lived a young shepherd boy whose only job was to watch the sheep on the hill. The days were long and quiet, and the boy grew terribly bored. One afternoon, just for fun, he ran down the hill shouting, Wolf! Wolf! The villagers dropped everything and raced up to help him. But there was no wolf at all. The boy laughed and laughed at the worried faces around him. The villagers were not amused, and they walked back down, shaking their heads. But the boy thought it was the funniest thing he had ever seen. So a few days later, he did it again. Wolf! Wolf! he cried. Again the villagers rushed up the hill, and again there was nothing there. This time they were angry. Do not cry wolf when there is no wolf, the oldest villager warned him. But what happened next, the boy never saw coming. That very evening, as the sky turned orange, a real wolf crept out from the dark trees. Its eyes were hungry, and it moved straight toward the frightened sheep. The boy jumped up and screamed with all his might, Wolf! Wolf! Please, come quickly! Down in the village, the people heard him. But they only sighed. He is fooling us again, they said, and no one came. The boy stood alone as the wolf scattered his flock across the hill. He had told the truth at last, but because he had lied so many times before, not a single person believed him. That night he learned a lesson he would never forget. The moral of the story is that no one believes a liar, even when they tell the truth. So always be honest, because your word is the most valuable thing you own. stories.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
stories.hook: While everyone else was playing, one tiny ant knew a secret about the coming winter.
stories.moral: The moral of the story is that hard work today protects you tomorrow.
stories.text: While everyone else was playing, one tiny ant knew a secret about the coming winter. It was a warm and golden summer, and in the tall grass lived a cheerful grasshopper who did nothing but sing and dance all day long. Nearby, a small ant marched back and forth, carrying crumbs of food far bigger than herself, storing them away grain by grain. The grasshopper laughed at her. Why do you work so hard on such a beautiful day? he chirped. Come and play with me instead! The ant wiped her brow and answered kindly, I am storing food for the winter, and I think you should do the same. The grasshopper only hopped away, giggling. There is plenty of time, he said. Summer will last forever. But summer does not last forever. Slowly the days grew shorter, the wind grew colder, and the green grass turned brown. Then one morning, soft white snow began to fall, covering every field and flower. The grasshopper shivered. He searched and searched, but there was no food anywhere. His stomach ached, and his legs trembled in the cold. At last he remembered the busy little ant. He knocked weakly on her cozy door. When the ant opened it, warm light and the smell of food spilled out. The grasshopper lowered his head in shame. I laughed at you, he whispered, but you were right all along. The kind ant did not scold him. She simply welcomed him inside, shared her food, and let him rest by the fire. And from that winter on, the grasshopper never wasted another summer day. The moral of the story is that hard work today protects you tomorrow. So prepare while you can, and a little effort now will save you from great trouble later. stories.title: The Lion and the Grateful Mouse
stories.hook: How could the smallest creature in the jungle ever save the mightiest king?
stories.moral: The moral of the story is that no act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.
stories.text: How could the smallest creature in the jungle ever save the mightiest king? Deep in the warm jungle, a great lion lay sleeping in the shade. He was the king of all the land, strong and proud. As he slept, a tiny mouse scurried across his enormous paw by accident and woke him with a start. In a flash, the lion's huge claws closed around the trembling little mouse. Please, squeaked the mouse, please let me go. One day I may be able to help you. The lion roared with laughter. How could a tiny thing like you ever help a king like me? But he was in a generous mood, so he lifted his paw and let the mouse run free. The mouse thanked him and disappeared into the grass. Some weeks later, the lion was prowling through the trees when he stepped into a hunter's trap. A thick rope net snapped up around him, lifting him off the ground. He roared and struggled, but the more he fought, the tighter the ropes held him. His mighty strength was useless. Then, through the leaves, came the patter of tiny feet. It was the little mouse. Do not worry, the mouse said, I have not forgotten you. With his sharp little teeth, the mouse began to gnaw at the ropes, one strand at a time. He worked all through the night, until at last the net fell away and the great lion was free. The proud king lowered his head to his tiny friend. I was wrong to laugh at you, he said softly. You have saved my life. The moral of the story is that no act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted. So be kind to everyone, for even the smallest friend can become the greatest help.
